system.name: Orient Anything V2
system.one_liner: Foundation model for 3D object orientation, rotational symmetry and relative rotation from one or two images, trained on synthesized 3D assets.

content.variant_note: three titled columns for the data engine, the model and the new capabilities, the last one a photo grid with drawn 3D axes
content.argues: The orientation foundation model is upgraded on both data (synthetic assets with fine labels) and model (joint encoder), gaining symmetry handling and relative rotation.
content.subject: Data-engine chain, joint-encoder diagram with one or two input images, and a grid of photos overlaid with 3D axes.

lessons.what_to_learn: Split the overview into three titled columns - how the data is made, how the model is built, what it can now do - and make the last column a grid of real results, so the claims of the first two are cashed out visually. Short italic property bullets beside each pipeline artifact state what the stage guarantees.
lessons.suits: Foundation-model or data-centric papers that contribute a data engine, a model change and new capabilities whose results can be shown on photos.

sections: Figure 1 on p.1 (caption and abstract only; no body paragraph mentions it)
evidence: Overview of Orient Anything V2. We upgrade the foundation orientation estimation model from both Data and Model perspectives.
gaining the New Features to handle rotational symmetry and relative rotation.
A multi-frame architecture that directly predicts relative object rotations.

summary: Orient Anything V2 is a foundation model that estimates the 3D orientation of an object, its rotational symmetry and the relative rotation between two views. Figure 1 is a three-part overview titled Data, Model and New Features. On the left a bottom-up data engine runs from Class Names through a generative model to 3D Assets, then through a pseudo ensemble to Fine Labels, with italic property bullets beside each artifact. In the middle a Joint Encoder sits above two weight-sharing Encoders: a solid path from one robot image gives Absolute Orientation and a dashed path from a second image gives Relative Rotation. On the right a grid of object photos carries drawn 3D axes, with two paired rows showing relative rotation.
summary_zh: Orient Anything V2 估计物体朝向、旋转对称和相对旋转。图 1 分三列：左为自下而上的数据引擎（类别名到精细标签），中为联合编码器（实线出绝对朝向、虚线出相对旋转），右为叠加三维坐标轴的照片网格。
notes: No body paragraph mentions the figure, so the roles of Pseudo ensemble (annotation) and of the dashed path (second frame, relative rotation) are read from the caption, abstract and drawing. A #4472c4 fill in the digest belongs to four rectangles hidden under the pair pictures and is not visible. The caption asks the reader to zoom in.
